draft.title: Inclusion and exclusion
card: being able to take part fully in society. A person who is included can join in work, use services, have a say in decisions and share in social life.
being shut out of work, services, decisions or social life. It is about being kept from taking part, not only about being alone.
Inclusion and exclusion are about access and taking part. They are not about whether a person has a few friends or feels shy.
A person can be included in some parts of life and excluded from others. For example, someone may have a job but be unable to use a local health service.
draft.remember: Inclusion is taking part fully. Exclusion is being shut out of parts of society.

a.q: Which situation is the best example of social exclusion?
opts: No accessible transport stops wheelchair users reaching work
A teenager in Bathurst chooses to spend weekends reading
A new worker in Perth spends a week learning office routines
A family in Cairns moves house and changes local school
a.why: The wheelchair users are kept from work by a barrier, so they are shut out of taking part. The teenager who chooses to stay home is not shut out by anyone, so that is not exclusion.
a.clue: Look for the person being kept out of work, services, decisions or social life.

b.q: Nina works full time in Dubbo and has many friends. The only doctor who speaks her language is in Sydney, so she cannot get health care she understands. Which statement is correct?
opts: She is included in work and friends but shut out of a service
She is fully included, because she has a job and many friends
She is fully excluded, because she cannot use one service
She is included, because exclusion is about being lonely
b.why: Nina takes part in work and social life, but she is shut out of a service she needs. The card says a person can be included in some parts of life and excluded from others. Calling her fully included ignores the service she cannot use.
b.clue: Check each area of life separately: work, services, decisions and social life.
